scope: Corollary 8.1 (Certified winning regions and strategies) of the manuscript “Randomized quasipolynomial-time mean-payoff games” (preprints/Randomized-quasipolynomial-time-mean-payoff-games-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 104 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4ab7552f58266134), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 37. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a randomized algorithm which, on every tape, uses 2O((log2(L+2))2) bit operations and returns either a failure symbol or the exact winning set together with an integer potential and positional strategies for both players. Whenever it returns these objects, the Max strategy wins from every vertex of the winning set and the Min strategy ensures upper limiting average at most −1/n from every other vertex, against arbitrary opposing strategies. It returns these objects with probability at least 7/8. Repeating independent trials until a certificate is accepted terminates almost surely, never returns an incorrect answer, and has expected bit cost 2O((log2(L+2))2).
